title: Assemble a sales report

outcomes.can: Predict the shape of a report built in steps.
Summarize orders and revenue by month.
Summarize sales by category, keeping products that never sold.
Label every customer by what they have spent.

intro: A report is several small answers joined together. This module assembles a sales report from the pieces of the earlier modules: totals worked out in steps, joins that keep rows with nothing sold, labels made with CASE, and counts that are safe from fan-out.

steps.title: Build a report from steps
steps.text: Start a report by naming its rows: one row per month, per category, per customer. That decides the GROUP BY of the last step. Then work backwards. Each number the report needs becomes a small step that produces one row per thing, with one total. Join the steps at the end. Totals from different tables go in different steps, so that joining them cannot multiply rows. Use a LEFT JOIN from the list of things the report must show, so a row with nothing to total still appears, and COALESCE its total to 0.

steps.title: Predict the result
steps.text: The step totals each customer's orders. The main query starts from customers with an id of 16 or more. Predict how many rows come back.

steps.title: Trace the result
steps.text: Five customers have an id of 16 or more, and the LEFT JOIN keeps all five. Two of them have orders and show a count. The other three have no row in the step, so the join leaves NULL, and COALESCE turns it into 0. The report's rows come from customers, not from orders, which is why nobody is missing.

choices.feedback: The LEFT JOIN keeps the customers who have no row in the step.
The step has one row per customer, and the main query starts from five customers.

review.evidence: Open a fresh starter on a later visit, with the earlier answer closed. A first unaided pass on every case is later evidence of the skill. A hinted pass stays recorded as assisted.

drillGap: These drills practise single features. They do not combine steps, labels and safe counts in one report.
